title: Harness or scorer mismatch
statement: Some apparent GLM failures originate in request projection or evaluation rather than generated behavior.
mechanism: A declared contract can differ from the delivered request; a scorer may reject valid behavior.
counterevidence: The recorded 19 schema failures agree with canonical reanalysis, which weakens a schema-scorer explanation.
falsifier: Audit finds no request-contract mismatch and independent semantic oracles agree on every selected counterexample.
baseline: Hash-bound request, response, validator and public-check receipts.
treatment: Independent audit of delivered schema plus mutation-tested semantic oracle; no model call.
prediction: Any disagreement is localized to exact bytes; do not credit a model improvement.
evidence: Frozen qualification traces and public counterexamples; source hashes matched for all 19 schema failures.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Output-contract burden
statement: Asking GLM to regenerate invariant envelope metadata causes avoidable initial schema omissions.
mechanism: Constant administrative fields compete with code generation; a prompt card or host-owned envelope may reduce omissions.
counterevidence: 17 of 19 schema-invalid proposals passed public behavior, but this does not identify why fields were omitted.
falsifier: On held-out tasks, explicit metadata guidance does not reduce raw omissions; a host envelope merely masks them without improving useful task success.
treatment: Separate arms: explicit metadata correction card; minimal model payload with deterministic host envelope and full final-schema validation.
prediction: Compare raw model fidelity separately from host-normalized validity; require semantic non-regression.
evidence: 18 missing schema_version and one missing authority_effect across 180 qualification trials.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Boundary reasoning
statement: GLM fails to apply boundary invariants even when the necessary facts are available.
mechanism: Explicit decision facts and a targeted boundary checklist may help it apply empty-history and interval rules.
counterevidence: Task differences may instead reflect prompt placement, task difficulty or transport exposure.
falsifier: A boundary card fails to improve unseen boundary cases against a matched-length neutral reminder, or gains require exposing expected answers.
baseline: Existing prompt plus neutral reminder of matched token length.
treatment: Task-specific correction card stating invariants, without fixture answers; hold information and output schema fixed.
prediction: Initial semantic success improves on held-out boundary variants; ordinary cases do not regress.
evidence: Public failures include start-boundary five times and empty-history four times; two semantic failures overlap schema defects.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Input representation
statement: A structured input representation can improve useful work per token under small soft windows.
mechanism: GCF may reduce encoding overhead, but explicit summaries or supplied counts can also explain apparent gains.
counterevidence: No local GLM/GCF result exists; the 8K/10K/12K outcomes are not monotonic.
falsifier: GCF gains vanish against compact JSON with identical facts and summaries, or codec savings do not reduce whole-request tokens without semantic regression.
baseline: Compact JSON, same facts and ordering.
treatment: Factorial compact JSON/GCF by summary absent/present; equal information in each encoding pair, unchanged output contract.
prediction: Prove round-trip equivalence first; compare full-request tokens, initial correctness and latency, not payload bytes alone.
evidence: Pinned GCF review is external mechanism evidence only; all local qualification used existing representation.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Continuity coverage
statement: Passing recorded recycling continuity can conceal loss of facts needed for later decisions.
mechanism: Current probes may cover delivery and selected invariants without testing delayed, conflicting or revised facts.
counterevidence: 43 of 43 actually recycled qualification trials passed; no nonpositive headroom was recorded.
falsifier: Expanded delayed and revised-fact probes agree with the existing metric across forced recycling, including deliberately corrupted replay negative controls.
treatment: Offline mutation probes deleting or corrupting required facts, then fresh delayed-fact tasks before/after forced recycling.
prediction: Metric rejects all declared corruptions before interpreting live retention scores; provider-internal compaction remains unobservable.
evidence: 12K qualification did not exercise recycling; 8K had 28 and 10K had 15 recycled trials.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Transport exposure
statement: Remaining transport failures reflect provider or network conditions more than model reasoning quality.
mechanism: Request duration, size, concurrency and time block affect timeout exposure; retry can rescue delivery independently of correctness.
counterevidence: We lack queue/network/inference timing separation; request size may still contribute.
falsifier: Failures reproduce by payload size within randomized time blocks while matched requests remain reliable, weakening a primarily time-condition explanation.
baseline: Frozen transport policy and receipt accounting.
treatment: Interleave matched payload-size groups by time block with fixed timeout, concurrency and retry cap; retain every failure.
prediction: Estimate failure rate by size and time block, report unknown usage and separate first response from recovered delivery.
evidence: Transport accounts for seven of eight final failures across the five campaigns.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?

title: Narrow-corpus optimism
statement: Repeated selection on four known task families overstates how well the candidate generalizes.
mechanism: Familiar fixtures and sequential candidate selection can improve final scores without broad initial capability.
counterevidence: Latest campaign passed 36/36 finally, but 28/36 initially; no held-out family estimate exists.
falsifier: A frozen candidate retains comparable initial and final performance on genuinely unseen task families across prespecified repetitions.
baseline: Frozen current candidate on known task families.
treatment: Same candidate and budgets on newly selected repository task families; keep development examples disjoint and freeze before calls.
prediction: Report held-out initial/final scores by family and window with uncertainty; never replace failed trials.
evidence: 467 exports represent 40 experiments but only four task families; 180 qualification trials are repeated known tasks.
controls: Freeze source, fixture, prompt, scorer and budget hashes before execution.
Separate initial response, correction, transport retry and final verification.
Preserve all failed and missing observations; do not pool changing candidates.
open_questions: What effect size and sample size are justified after the offline audit?
